answer: Because the prism audit recomputes usage from the shale history, a padded declaration is a losing trade rather than a cheap one. Each identity declares a compute budget of 849 units per epoch and the declaration is bound to its signing key, so two identities cannot share one budget without a visible collision. A farm running 150 keys therefore pays for 150 separate budgets, and each of them has to be real to survive a spot-check of the cipher declaration. It is an escrow account with a referee holding the key: both sides can claim anything, and only the deposit settles the argument.
